The required reduction of the density sink occurs over a highly localised region with the timescale of the density sink increased by a factor of 25
The transport is known to be highly non-diffusive [1, 2] which makes capturing it in typical 2D transport codes such as SOLPS [3], EDGE2D [4] or UEDGE [5] a challenge

Measurements on many tokamaks worldwide have revealed that SOL transport is intermittent [6, 7, 8, 9, 10], with this intermittency resulting from the radial propagation of coherent structures commonly termed blobs or filaments [11]
The propagation of a filament is a complex non-linear problem [12] for which numerical simulation is often required [13, 14, 15]
